title: Execution Cohort Playbook and Experiment Journal
author: Aisha Khatri
body:
Purpose
-----
This document describes the "execution cohort" concept we use to group similar inference requests for improved latency predictability and cost efficiency. It combines architecture notes, scheduling policy pseudocode, a profiling playbook for cohort-related regressions, a benchmarking experiment design, a release checklist, a curated known-issues list, and incident runbooks.

Audience
--------
- Runtime engineers implementing or tuning the scheduler and kernel selection.
- SREs owning runtime availability and alerting.
- Applied ML engineers designing workload-fit experiments.

Goals and success criteria
--------------------------
- Reduce P99 tail latency variance for small/interactive models by >= 20% versus baseline.
- Maintain per-tenant throughput within 10% of historical baseline while reducing per-token cost.
- Provide deterministic, reproducible experiment artifacts for every scheduling change.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
- In scope: cohort creation heuristics, scheduling policy, kernel dispatch interaction, profiling and benchmark plans, runbook steps for cohort incidents.
- Not in scope: model quantization strategy, private-deployment network setup (see eng-private-deployments docs).

Architecture overview (text diagram)
-----------------------------------
Key services and components involved:
- runtime-cohort-manager (component that classifies incoming requests into cohorts)
- kernel-dispatcher (maps scheduled slots to GPU kernels/queues)
- kv-cache-proxy (shared KV cache service for prefix reuse)
- scheduler-ledger (global admission controller and capacity accounting)
- telemetry-ingest (traces, events, metrics pipeline)

Simple ASCII diagram:

  client -> ingress-router -> runtime-cohort-manager --+--> scheduler-ledger --> kernel-dispatcher --> GPU
                                                       |\
                                                       +--> kv-cache-proxy (hot prefix reuse)

Design intent:
- Cohorts are immutable for the lifetime of a request. Classification is cheap and stable (hash + lightweight fingerprint).
- Scheduler decisions are made at cohort granularity (batching, priority, slot reservation).
- The kernel-dispatcher uses cohort metadata to select optimized kernels and execution paths (e.g., fused-attention, reduced-precision path).

Cohort definition and metadata fields
------------------------------------
Each cohort record contains flat fields used by multiple subsystems:
- cohort_id (string)
- workload_family (string, e.g., "chat-short", "embedding-long")
- model_variant (string)
- target_slo_ms (numeric as string, e.g., "120")
- prefer_low_latency (true/false as string)
- suggested_batching (string, e.g., "auto|max_tokens:64|min_batch:1")
- kv_cache_key_hint (short string)
- owner (team/email)

Cohort lifecycle
----------------
1. Classification: runtime-cohort-manager computes fingerprint and assigns cohort_id.
2. Admission: scheduler-ledger evaluates slot credits and admission rules.
3. Dispatch: kernel-dispatcher picks the kernel path and queue.
4. Post-process: telemetry-ingest tags traces with cohort_id and quality signals.

Priority and fairness policy (plain-language)
-------------------------------------------
- Priority is a function of (SLO attainment delta, observed tail risk, tenant SLAs).
- Fairness is enforced by token-based credit accounting in scheduler-ledger.
- Emergency preemption rules: high-priority control-plane traffic and SLA-protected cohorts can preempt best-effort cohorts up to a configured cap (default 15% of active slots).

Scheduling policy pseudocode
----------------------------
// Simplified view used in design discussions
function admit_request(request):
  cohort = classify(request)
  credits = ledger.peek_credits(cohort.owner)
  if credits < cohort.min_credit_threshold:
    if cohort.prefer_low_latency == "true":
      // try fast-path hedging up to X times
      return try_fast_path_hedge(request, cohort)
    else:
      return queue_in_backlog(request, cohort)
  // apply latency headroom check
  estimated_latency = kernel_dispatcher.estimate_latency(cohort, request.tokens)
  if estimated_latency <= cohort.target_slo_ms * 1.2:
    ledger.consume(credits, estimate_cost(request))
    return schedule_on_queue(request, cohort.preferred_queue)
  else:
    return fallback_to_variant_or_degrade(request)

Key tunables (table)
--------------------
- min_credit_threshold: smallest credit bucket to allow admission (default "5").
- hedging_max_attempts: max hedges for low-latency cohorts (default "2").
- preemption_cap_pct: percentage of slots reclaimable for SLAs (default "15").
- kv_prefetch_window_ms: how far ahead to warm prefix cache (default "200").

Profiling playbook for cohort regressions
---------------------------------------
When a cohort shows increased tail latency or error rate, follow these steps:
1. Capture a deterministic traffic sample (10k requests) by inserting a traffic mirror rule for cohort_id.
2. Run lightweight traces: set telemetry-ingest sampling to 100% for cohort_id for 1 minute.
3. Collect kernel-level timelines: use kernel-trace-tool "ktctl sample --cohort <id> --duration 60s --out /tmp/kt.json".
4. Correlate traces with ledger events: ledger.trace_id -> kernel-trace -> application trace.
5. If KV cache miss rate > 30% for the cohort, run kv-cache-warmup script and re-evaluate.
6. If kernel queuing time accounts for >50% of tail latency, escalate to kernel team with attached kt.json and sampled traces.

Profiling commands and quick checks
----------------------------------
- Check admission backlog: curl -s http://scheduler-ledger.local/metrics | jq '.backlog_by_cohort["<cohort_id>"]'
- Kernel queue times: ktctl histogram --cohort <id> --metric queue_ms
- KV cache hit ratio: curl http://kv-cache-proxy/metrics | grep cohort_<id>_hit_ratio

Benchmarking experiment design (template)
---------------------------------------
Objective: evaluate impact of cohort-aware scheduling on tail latency and cost.
Experiment matrix (examples):
- Variables: batch_size {1,4,8}, concurrency_shape {steady, bursty-10s, spiky-1s}, model_variant {v1, v1-quant}  
- Metrics: P50, P95, P99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec, tokens/cost, cohort_kv_hit_ratio, queue_time_ms.

Sample YAML workload config:
```yaml
workload_name: chat-short-burst-test
model: gptx-chat-v1
cohort_label: chat-short
duration_s: 900
phases:
  - name: warmup
    qps: 50
    duration_s: 120
  - name: burst
    qps: 1200
    duration_s: 30
  - name: steady
    qps: 200
    duration_s: 660
request_shape:
  avg_tokens: 48
  seed_variability: high
batch_policy:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 256
  max_batch_requests: 8
```

Benchmark collection checklist:
- Mirror production ingress for the cohort (shadow-mode)
- Collect kernel-trace logs (ktctl) and telemetry traces for entire run
- Snapshot scheduler-ledger state before/after test
- Record cost estimate via runtime-cost-sim tool

Release checklist for scheduler/cohort changes
--------------------------------------------
1. Update unit tests for scheduler policy language and cohort classification.
2. Run local microbenchmarks (microbench-suite) and record baseline artifacts.
3. Create canary branch with new policy and schedule canary deployment across 1% of requests for 24 hours.
4. Monitor KPIs: P95, P99, queue_time_ms, kernel_queue_depth, error_rate.
5. If regressions are detected, revert using feature-flag rollback or scale down new variants.
6. Post-mortem experiment: reproduce with synthetic workload within 72 hours.

Known issues (curated)
---------------------
1) Cohort oscillation under mixed bursty traffic
- Symptom: cohort membership toggles for identical request fingerprints leading to cache fragmentation.
- Probable root cause: fingerprint window too short (default 30s).
- Mitigation: increase fingerprint stability window to 5 minutes for high-throughput cohorts; schedule a follow-up stability test.

2) Hedging-created duplicate kernel load
- Symptom: hedged fast-path attempts increase GPU occupancy and raise queue times for best-effort cohorts.
- Root cause: lack of cross-cohort hedging circuit-breaker.
- Mitigation: enforce global_hedge_inflight limit and introduce per-node hedging accounting.

3) KV prefetch storm on rollout
- Symptom: massive KV warmups when a variant is rolled out, causing transient I/O saturation.
- Root cause: naive prefetch for all cohorts on deploy.
- Mitigation: stagger kv_prefetch_window and use probabilistic prefetch sampling (10% initially).

4) Scheduler-ledger stale view after partial-network-partition
- Symptom: admission decisions based on outdated credits causing over-admission.
- Root cause: optimistic-local-ledger without timely reconciliation.
- Mitigation: enable short reconciliation heartbeat (default 2s) and fall back to conservative admission if heartbeat missed > 3x.

Runbook: Cohort starvation incident
----------------------------------
Trigger: alert "cohort_p99_latency > 2x target for 5 minutes" or backlog growth > 5000 requests.
Immediate steps (0–5 minutes):
1. Pager to oncall runtime engineer.
2. Run quick health checks:
   - curl http://scheduler-ledger.local/health
   - ktctl histogram --cohort <id> --metric queue_ms --last 5m
3. If kernel queue_ms > 300ms and backlog growing, scale temporary admission down: curl -XPOST http://scheduler-ledger.local/actuate "{\"action\":\"throttle_cohort\",\"cohort\":\"<id>\",\"pct\":\"50\"}"
4. If KV miss ratio > 40%, trigger kv-cache warmup and allocate one prefetch worker: kvprefetchctl start --cohort <id> --workers 1
5. If situation persists beyond 15 minutes, revert recent scheduler changes (feature flag) and roll back canary.

Post-incident actions (within 72 hours):
- Run profiling playbook and attach artifacts to incident ticket.
- Schedule a postmortem and update cohort stability parameters.

Telemetry and dashboards (recommended)
-------------------------------------
Essential metrics (metric names follow internal conventions):
- cohort.<cohort_id>.p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms
- cohort.<cohort_id>.queue_time_ms
- cohort.<cohort_id>.kv_hit_ratio
- scheduler.ledger.backlog_by_cohort
- kernel.queue_depth, kernel.exec_time_ms_histogram
- runtime.coalesced_batch_size_by_cohort

Suggested alert thresholds (example)
- cohort.<id>.p99_ms > target_slo_ms * 2 for 5m -> P1
- cohort.<id>.kv_hit_ratio < 0.5 for 10m -> P2
- scheduler.ledger.backlog_by_cohort > 1000 -> P1

Experiment journal template (copy into new experiment ticket)
------------------------------------------------------------
- experiment_id: (auto)
- lead: name/email
- hypothesis: short sentence
- cohort_ids: list
- config_snapshot: (link to S3 / artifact)
- benchmark_matrix: (variables & ranges)
- start_time / end_time
- raw_artifacts: list of links (ktctl, traces, ledger snapshots)
- outcome: pass/fail/observations
- followups: actionable items

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- runtime-cohort-manager: @runtime-team (primary)
- kernel-dispatcher: @kernels-team (secondary)
- scheduler-ledger: @sre-runtime
- telemetry and traces: @observability

Appendix: quick reference commands
---------------------------------
- classify example: curl -XPOST http://runtime-cohort-manager/classify -d '{"request": "..."}'
- ledger peek: curl http://scheduler-ledger.local/credits?owner=<team>
- start a focused trace: tracectl start --filter cohort_id=<id> --duration 60s
- canary rollback: ffctl disable feature.scheduler_new_policy
